items.title: Sequential likelihood-ratio test
items.statement:
Assume the [[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]], which states that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0})$ be a discrete filtration on a common measurable space and let $P_0,P_1$ be probability measures on it. Assume that for every $t\ge0$, the restrictions $P_0|_{\mathcal F_t}$ and $P_1|_{\mathcal F_t}$ are mutually absolutely continuous: each restriction assigns measure zero to exactly the same $\mathcal F_t$ events as the other. For each $t$, choose a nonnegative $\mathcal F_t$-measurable representative $L_t$ of the likelihood-ratio density $d(P_1|_{\mathcal F_t})/d(P_0|_{\mathcal F_t})$ [[def-likelihood-ratio-as-rn-derivative]]. The filtration and stopping-time conventions are those of [[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]] and [[def-discrete-stopping-time]].

Input thresholds $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1)$. At times $t=1,2,\ldots$, compute $L_t$ and apply these instructions:

1. If $L_t\ge1/\alpha$, stop and decide $H_1$.
2. Otherwise, if $L_t\le\beta$, stop and decide $H_0$.
3. Otherwise continue to the next observation.

The two boundaries are disjoint because $\beta<1<1/\alpha$. The output time is
$$\tau=\inf\{t\ge1:L_t\ge1/\alpha\text{ or }L_t\le\beta\},\qquad \inf\varnothing=\infty.$$
If $\tau=\infty$, the procedure has no finite terminal decision. It does not itself assert that a crossing occurs.

references.title: Robert L. Wolpert, Introduction to Martingales, STA 711 course notes, §1.2, PDF pp. 4–5

items.title: Finite-sample likelihood ratio for iid observations
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P_0,P_1$ be probability measures on a common measurable space and let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be random elements of $(S,\Sigma)$ that are IID under each $P_j$, with one-coordinate law $Q_j$. Suppose $Q_1\ll Q_0$, let $\lambda=dQ_1/dQ_0$ be a nonnegative representative, and put $\mathcal F_t=\sigma(X_1,\ldots,X_t)$. For every $t\ge1$,
$$L_t:=\prod_{i=1}^t\lambda(X_i)$$
is a version of $d(P_1|_{\mathcal F_t})/d(P_0|_{\mathcal F_t})$.

references.title: Robert L. Wolpert, Introduction to Martingales, STA 711 course notes, §1.2, PDF p. 4
Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., §2.1.2, Theorem 2.1.11, printed p. 48

items.title: Terminal error bounds for a sequential likelihood-ratio test
items.statement:
Assume AC. Under the hypotheses of [[alg-sequential-likelihood-ratio-test]], the boundary rule $\tau$ is a stopping time and, for the specified decisions,
$$P_0(\tau<\infty,\ L_\tau\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha,\qquad P_1(\tau<\infty,\ L_\tau\le\beta)\le\beta.$$
These bounds concern terminal errors and do not assume that $\tau$ is finite almost surely.

references.title: Robert L. Wolpert, Introduction to Martingales, STA 711 course notes, §1.2, PDF pp. 4–5
Steven R. Howard, Aaditya Ramdas, Jon McAuliffe and Jasjeet Sekhon, Time-uniform Chernoff bounds via nonnegative supermartingales, Probability Surveys 17 (2020), Lemma 1 and proof, PDF pp. 15 and 45

items.title: Iid drift conditions imply almost-sure test termination
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be IID under each of two probability measures $P_j$, with one-coordinate law $Q_j$, and suppose $Q_0$ and $Q_1$ are equivalent. Choose a finite strictly positive representative $\lambda=dQ_1/dQ_0$ and set $Z=\log\lambda$. If
$$\mathbb E_{Q_0}|Z|,\mathbb E_{Q_1}|Z|<\infty,\qquad \mathbb E_{Q_0}Z<0<\mathbb E_{Q_1}Z,$$
then for every $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1)$ the algorithm [[alg-sequential-likelihood-ratio-test]], with $\mathcal F_0=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}$ and $\mathcal F_t=\sigma(X_1,\ldots,X_t)$, satisfies
$$P_0(\tau<\infty)=P_1(\tau<\infty)=1.$$

references.title: Robert L. Wolpert, Introduction to Martingales, STA 711 course notes, §1.2, PDF p. 4
Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., §2.4, Theorem 2.4.1 and proof, printed pp. 76–78

items.title: Exact Bernoulli crossings in a sequential likelihood-ratio test
items.statement: Assume AC. Consider IID observations $X_i\in\{0,1\}$. Under $H_0$, let $P_0(X_i=1)=1/4$; under $H_1$, let $P_1(X_i=1)=3/4$. Use the procedure [[alg-sequential-likelihood-ratio-test]] with $\alpha=\beta=1/4$. A type-I error means deciding $H_1$ when $P_0$ governs the observations; a type-II error means deciding $H_0$ when $P_1$ governs them. The terminal type-I and type-II error probabilities are each $1/10$, and the test stops almost surely under either law.
